fieldMarks: Rotund rodent 26–36 cm plus a 20–28 cm scaly, rat-like tail; 0.9–1.8 kg
Silvery to dark brown glossy coat with a lighter belly; dark feet and tail
Hind feet large but not webbed, fringed with stiff hairs
behavior: Builds dome houses of cattail and bulrush 0.6–0.9 m high, or tunnels into banks
In winter feeds under the ice and builds 'pushups' of vegetation over holes
Mainly eats roots and stems of cattails, lilies, sedges and grasses; occasionally mussels and small fish
Leaves musky scent at stations and makes slides and channels through bank vegetation
habitat: Freshwater marshes, marshy lake edges and slow streams with water deep enough not to freeze to the bottom but shallow enough for aquatic plants (ideally 1–2 m).
range: North America north to the treeline, including Newfoundland, south to the Gulf Coast, Rio Grande and lower Colorado River; introduced in Eurasia and Argentina.

lookalikes.name: Beaver
lookalikes.howToTell: The muskrat is much smaller with a rat-like tail rather than a broad flat one.

lookalikes.name: Nutria
lookalikes.howToTell: Nutria are much larger with a round tail and white whiskers; muskrats have a side-flattened tail and no webbing between the toes.
